Title:
LoopBridge: Should Prefill and Decode Loop Equally?

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
26 pages, 14 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one block of layers for the same number of loops during prefill and decode. Yet generation is heavily asymmetric: prefill reads the prompt once in parallel and takes under 3% of the time, while decoding runs per token and takes over 97%. We show that prefill and decode should not loop equally. Instead, we untie the two loop counts - reading the prompt with more loops and decoding each token with fewer - and introduce LoopBridge, a lightweight adapter (at most 2.4% of the parameters) with RoPE-commuting key-value maps that bridges any trained prefill/decode pair and folds into the prompt cache at prefill. On Ouro-2.6B at one decode loop, four prefill loops lift the 11-benchmark average from 44.2 to 58.6 (fixed prefill depth) and 58.2 (LoopBridge), far above tied-loop distillation on the same data (49.5). On Ouro-2.6B-Thinking GSM8K, LoopBridge with four prefill and two decode loops matches the four-loop model's accuracy at 2.0x the end-to-end throughput. These gains peak at two to five prefill loops and transfer to Ouro-1.4B, Thinking models and looped decision models. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode
